parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
Fig. 6.1 shows the concentration of four hormones in a woman's blood during one menstrual cycle.
{{figure:figure_6_1.png}}
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 6.1, explain why there is a large increase in LH at around day 12.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State how Fig. 6.1 shows that the woman did not become pregnant during this cycle.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The combined oral contraceptive pill contains oestrogen and progesterone.
parts.text: Explain how this combined contraceptive pill works to prevent pregnancy.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why some women take the combined contraceptive pill for just the first 21 days of their cycles.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Some women have a contraceptive device inserted under the skin. This releases hormones into the blood and can last for up to three years.

Suggest **one** advantage of using such a device rather than taking contraceptive pills.
